sources.entry: Hop - Eighteen everyday tools in one menu bar panel: timer, time tracker, keep-awake, system monitor, clipboard history, file converter, window manager, torrents, archives, text recognition, screenshots with an editor, drawing over the screen, color picker, VPN switcher, app launcher, app uninstaller, keyboard lock and internet speed test. Native, offline, no telemetry.

summary.one_liner: Hop is a free, native macOS menu bar app that bundles many small utilities (timer, time tracker, keep-awake, system monitor, clipboard history, file converter, screenshots, and more) into one panel with up to four tabs.
summary.what_it_does: Hop lives in the macOS menu bar and lets you switch on the modules you need, arranging them across up to four tabs on the icon. Included modules cover a Pomodoro-style timer with work-rest cycles, a time tracker with projects and a to-do list, a keep-awake sleep blocker, a system monitor for CPU, GPU, memory, network, disk and battery, and a clipboard history of recent text, images and files. It also has a file converter for images, PDFs, video and audio, a window snapper, a lite BitTorrent client, archive unpacking and packing (zip, rar, 7z, tar variants), screenshots with an editor, on-screen drawing, text recognition using Apple's Vision, a color picker, a keyboard lock, a VPN switcher, an app launcher, an app uninstaller, traffic blocking via a macOS network filter, sound device control, and an internet speed test using macOS networkQuality. The README states it collects no telemetry and runs locally, touching the network only for update checks, the speed test, and optional torrent engine download.
use_cases: replace several small menu bar utilities with one app
convert images, PDFs and videos on a Mac
track time spent on tasks and projects
keep a Mac awake during downloads or builds
block network connections from specific apps
how_to_run: Download Hop.dmg from the releases and drag Hop.app into Applications
Building from source: git clone the repository, then cd hop
notable: Up to 18 modules in one menu bar panel, arranged across four tabs
Traffic blocking uses the macOS network filter, similar in approach to LuLu and Little Snitch
VPN switcher reads the VPN list from system settings automatically
Uninstaller moves app leftovers to the Trash rather than deleting them
Signed with Apple Developer ID and notarized; updates verified with Ed25519
caveats: Torrent engine (~26 MB), rar/7z helpers (~6 MB) and MKV/WebM helper are separate downloads, and the torrent module is off by default
Updating to 1.10.0 cleared all permissions, which had to be granted again
